A1.justification: Both 29-page PDFs describe CoMiGS and include the main paper and Appendices A-F. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original GPT2 and Llama fine-tuning experiments, including baseline perplexities, ablations, resource-heterogeneity experiments and routing analyses in Section 4 and Appendices C-E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and outcomes, including the numerical comparisons in Tables 1, 2, 5 and 6 and the routing and learning-curve analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same experts, routing, objectives, updates and aggregation procedure. Appendix F.4 changes the update restatement within its proof; the underlying procedure in Eq. (28) remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same next-token tasks on Multilingual Wikipedia, SlimPajama, AG News and the Common Corpus/patent-data setup. Language/category coverage and in-distribution and out-of-distribution scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2 and 5 retain their comparison methods, including PCL, pFedMoE, FDLoRA, HetLoRA, FlexLoRA, FFA-LoRA and FedSa-LoRA. The newly cited Almansoori et al. work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same model sizes, perplexity metric, token splits, training budgets and routing-update settings. The active/full-parameter matching controls for heterogeneous models also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The router-update ablations, load-balancing comparisons, data/resource mismatch experiments and token-routing case studies are retained. Section 4 and Appendices C-E add or remove no analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across three seeds in Tables 1, 2 and 5 and retain the same graphical uncertainty reporting. No run-count disclosure or statistical estimation procedure changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1-6 and the reported learning and routing results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains CoMiGS-1G1S perplexities of 47.19 (0.10) for GPT2 on Multilingual Wikipedia and 16.31 (0.05) for Llama on AG News.

T1.justification: Appendix F.3 corrects g2's interaction sign and replaces its erroneous Theta regularizer with a Phi regularizer, then explicitly decomposes the objective. F.4 reverses the displayed block-update order to align with the stationarity calculation in Eq. (29). These are localized proof revisions; assumptions and stated convergence rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about novelty, handling both kinds of heterogeneity, personalization, overfitting resistance, resource efficiency and convergence.

C2.justification: Interpretations of expert specialization and generalists' regularizing effect are unchanged. Both versions retain the limitation on preventing overfitting for easy tasks and the Impact Statement's privacy and adversarial-robustness qualifications.

D1.justification: The code-access information, hardware disclosures, learning rates, LoRA hyperparameters, routing schedules, token counts and baseline-tuning details remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B-C.

R1.justification: v4 adds Almansoori et al. (2024), Collaborative and Efficient Personalization with Mixtures of Adaptors, and briefly positions its mixture of generalists with local routers as resembling a simplified CoMiGS in Appendix F.3. Other reference edits update metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: v4 replaces the preprint notice with proceedings information, expands the funding acknowledgment, revises limited proof prose and consistently renames the unchanged simplex set. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 has small spacing and positioning adjustments. Publication information and expanded reference/proof text cause local reflow, including moving the start of F.4 to page 29. All figures and tables are retained without substantive display redesign.

improvement.justification: The corrected g2 expression and explicit decomposition in Appendix F.3 remove concrete inconsistencies and improve the proof's checkability; the added related-work acknowledgment improves attribution. These support a modest overall gain. The new assertion that log-sum-exp is strictly convex is overstated on its stated domain, although only convexity is needed for that decomposition argument.
